lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: route and schedule planning

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic route and schedule planning task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: In the fictional town of Cedar Hollow, a community garden supply booth at Riverside Market closes at 11:00 a.m.
materials: learner-local: the fictional Cedar Hollow map and Hollow Line bus schedule printed on this task sheet

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l01-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l01-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l01-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l01-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: If the 9:40 bus were 10 minutes late, would your plan from Task 3 still work? Explain what you would do differently.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g8-u04-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Reading and using the fictional schedule: Selects a departure time and correctly calculates ride time, walking time, and arrival time using only the schedule and map details as given. | Trip plan sequencing and completeness: Plan states leave-home time, bus departure, ride and walk duration, arrival time, and buffer in order, with a clear reason for the chosen departure. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner plan a second fictional route on the same Hollow Line schedule that arrives at Riverside Market by 9:30 instead of 11:00, using an earlier departure.

duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

resources.title: route and schedule planning worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: In the fictional town of Cedar Hollow, a community garden supply booth at Riverside Market closes at 11:00 a.m.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact route and schedule planning decision or action.
Model move 2: Read the fictional Hollow Line schedule below before planning anything.
Model move 3: Work out the walk on the home end of the trip before finalizing a leave-home time.

Model check: Reading and using the fictional schedule: Selects a departure time and correctly calculates ride time, walking time, and arrival time using only the schedule and map details as given. | Trip plan sequencing and completeness: Plan states leave-home time, bus departure, ride and walk duration, arrival time, and buffer in order, with a clear reason for the chosen departure.

resources.title: route and schedule planning action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for route and schedule planning.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: route and schedule planning coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: In the fictional town of Cedar Hollow, a community garden supply booth at Riverside Market closes at 11:00 a.m.
Coach direction: Read the fictional Hollow Line schedule below before planning anything.

Learner prompt: The Hollow Line Route 4 bus leaves the Oak Street stop at 9:10, 9:40, and 10:10 on Saturday mornings and takes 15 minutes to reach the Riverside Market stop. The walk from the Riverside Market stop to the garden supply booth takes 8 minutes, and the booth closes at 11:00 a.m. Which departure is the latest one that still gets the fictional errand-runner to the booth at least 15 minutes before closing, and why?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: route and schedule planning complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Work out the walk on the home end of the trip before finalizing a leave-home time.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I identified the correct starting bus stop and the correct arrival bus stop for this fictional trip.
Response 2 (t2-p2): Home is a 6-minute walk from the Oak Street stop. What time does the fictional errand-runner need to leave home to catch the departure you chose in Task 1?
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: route and schedule planning minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: If the 9:40 bus were 10 minutes late, would your plan from Task 3 still work? Explain what you would do differently.

Success checks: Reading and using the fictional schedule: Selects a departure time and correctly calculates ride time, walking time, and arrival time using only the schedule and map details as given. | Trip plan sequencing and completeness: Plan states leave-home time, bus departure, ride and walk duration, arrival time, and buffer in order, with a clear reason for the chosen departure.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: route and schedule planning supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l01-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g8-u04-l01-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional route and schedule planning condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Reading and using the fictional schedule: Selects a departure time and correctly calculates ride time, walking time, and arrival time using only the schedule and map details as given. | Trip plan sequencing and completeness: Plan states leave-home time, bus departure, ride and walk duration, arrival time, and buffer in order, with a clear reason for the chosen departure..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l01-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

Check against: Reading and using the fictional schedule: Selects a departure time and correctly calculates ride time, walking time, and arrival time using only the schedule and map details as given. | Trip plan sequencing and completeness: Plan states leave-home time, bus departure, ride and walk duration, arrival time, and buffer in order, with a clear reason for the chosen departure.

coachMoves: Ask the learner to name the condition.

simulationRoute.title: route and schedule planning — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the route and schedule planning task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: If the 9:40 bus were 10 minutes late, would your plan from Task 3 still work? Explain what you would do differently.
observableCriteria: Reading and using the fictional schedule: Selects a departure time and correctly calculates ride time, walking time, and arrival time using only the schedule and map details as given.
Trip plan sequencing and completeness: Plan states leave-home time, bus departure, ride and walk duration, arrival time, and buffer in order, with a clear reason for the chosen departure.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g8-u04-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Reading and using the fictional schedule: Selects a departure time and correctly calculates ride time, walking time, and arrival time using only the schedule and map details as given. | Trip plan sequencing and completeness: Plan states leave-home time, bus departure, ride and walk duration, arrival time, and buffer in order, with a clear reason for the chosen departure.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
